A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Layer Parallelism research. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original layer-intervention, perplexity, benchmark-accuracy, inference-timing, fine-tuning, and GPU-profiling results.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds activation-similarity measurements, further fine-tuning results, and four-GPU throughput measurements.

M1.justification: The evaluated LP procedure retains parallel attention, shared intermediate aggregation, parallel FFNs, original LayerNorms, and optional fine-tuning. The new LP equation explicitly describes the implementation already shown in v2 Figure 2 and Section 4. Merged LayerNorms are mentioned as exploratory alternatives, without replacing the evaluated procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use RedPajama and the same benchmark tasks, including MMLU, PIQA, ARC, WinoGrande, OpenBookQA, HellaSwag, GSM-8K, and IFEval. Added analyses and hardware/model configurations do not introduce different represented data or task requirements.

E2.justification: v3 Appendix B adds quantitative comparisons with Sync-Point Drop, selective low-bit communication, and MX compression, especially Table 3 alongside LP. These comparisons use literature-sourced results under heterogeneous models, hardware, and metrics; they do not establish new matched baseline runs. v2 lacks these competing optimization comparisons.

E3.justification: v3 adds standard-versus-counterfactual activation comparisons using CKA and decoding measurements on four A100 PCIe GPUs. Fine-tuning evaluation shifts from a training-step sweep at Qwen3-4B depth 27 to 4096-step evaluations across several Qwen3-4B and 14B depths. Table 1 also removes base-Llama and some aggressive Qwen configurations. The retained main benchmark protocol remains five-shot, with zero-shot IFEval.

E4.justification: New Figure 5 tests dependence on upstream residual contributions through activation similarity, and Appendix D empirically tests four-GPU scaling. Table 2 expands accuracy-recovery analysis across model sizes and depths while removing the earlier training-duration sweep. Existing perplexity, latency, throughput, and profiling analyses remain.

E5.justification: Tables 1 and 2 newly attach uncertainty-style numerical subscripts to accuracy estimates, whereas v2 reports point estimates alone. Their meaning and estimation procedure are not explained, and neither PDF specifies repeated-run counts or seeds; additional runs cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: Most retained Table 1 accuracy means are unchanged after conversion to percentages, but speed columns, CKA findings, and additional fine-tuned configurations are newly reported. Table 6 adds four-GPU throughput factors of 1.24, 1.34, and 1.46. Base-Llama benchmark rows, extreme Qwen configurations, and the 1024/8192-step tuning results disappear. Table 2 also updates Qwen3-4B baseline percentages from 70.14/58.87/85.14 to 70.16/58.79/84.99.

T1.justification: New Appendix A derives a first-order decomposition of LP approximation error, a Jacobian-based approximate bound, and error propagation through subsequent layers. It also develops arguments concerning layer selection and consecutive pairs. v2 provides computational equations and intuition but no corresponding error analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract replaces the broad 1.05–1.20x throughput and 95–99% accuracy-retention headline with a Llama2-7B-specific 1.19x gain and 1.5% accuracy reduction. The conclusion adds quantified depth and single-token speed claims. The central contributions of post-hoc LP and partial recovery through fine-tuning remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations connecting residual magnitude, Jacobian sensitivity, CKA, layer selection, and reasoning degradation. Appendix B discusses hardware dependence, competing communication optimizations, and explicitly unvalidated LP-plus-quantization benefits. Section 6 also qualifies the earlier suggestion of unavoidable accuracy loss by allowing that more involved fine-tuning might recover it.

D1.justification: v3 clarifies the implemented shared-intermediate computation, states an attention-head divisibility requirement, documents counterfactual activation construction, and supplies four-GPU hardware and timing-normalization information. Existing fine-tuning optimizer, learning rate, batch size, and data source remain. No new implementation-code access information is supplied.

R1.justification: New citations to SPD, low-bit communication, MX compression, and CKA accompany substantial positioning changes. Section 2 and Appendix B distinguish synchronization-count reduction from communication compression and compare their hardware and accuracy trade-offs. This considerably expands the discussion of directly relevant alternatives.

P1.justification: The abstract and selected introduction, related-work, fine-tuning, and conclusion passages are rewritten. Section 3 regroups shuffling, pruning, and merging discussion, and the Impact Statement is removed. The main seven-section organization remains, with existing appendices following two newly added ones.

P2.justification: v3 adopts the TMLR layout and substantially redesigns Tables 1 and 2, including speed, relative-performance, uncertainty, and grouped fine-tuning displays. It adds the CKA figure and four appendix tables. Earlier plots, diagrams, and profiling displays are largely retained with resizing, relocation, and renumbering.

improvement.justification: Clarifying the implemented LP computation and adding CKA, broader fine-tuning, and four-GPU measurements modestly strengthen explanation and empirical support. Benefits are tempered by removed base-model results and the training-step sweep, unexplained uncertainty annotations, and new reporting inconsistencies: Qwen3-4B depth-30 ARC-C is 52.39 in Table 1 but 50.43 in Table 2, while Appendix D uses layer-count notation inconsistently with Table 6.
